definition: Numba is a just-in-time compiler that turns numeric Python functions into fast machine code with one decorator.
details: Created at Continuum Analytics (now Anaconda) in 2012; community maintained.

explainer.lead: How to install Numba, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.inAi: Speed up custom loops — a distance metric, a simulation, a reward function — that NumPy cannot vectorise.
explainer.jsNote: Numba is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: You write an ordinary Python recipe and stick a label on it; the label tells a compiler to rewrite the recipe in machine language so it runs much faster.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers decorate hot numeric loops or functions with a Numba target so they are compiled at call time; a common pitfall is that code relying on unsupported Python features or dynamic types may fail to compile or slow down.
tiers.paperLevel: Numba performs type inference on a Python function and compiles a specialized machine-code version via LLVM, dispatching to it at runtime. Limits: works best on numeric, array-oriented code with types that can be inferred.

explainer.example: A loop summing over a NumPy array, once decorated, is compiled on first call and then runs as machine code on subsequent calls.
